title: fix(ci): use release payload tag for Docker publish
description:
## Summary
Fixes the release Docker publish job by using the GitHub Release payload tag instead of `github.ref_name` when setting the image version and Docker tag.

This prevents release builds from producing an empty Docker tag like:
```
safeglobal/safe-client-gateway-nest:
```

## Changes

Added `RELEASE_TAG` from `github.event.release.tag_name`
Updated release Docker `VERSION` build arg to use `RELEASE_TAG`
Updated release Docker image tag to use `RELEASE_TAG`

findings.claim: The step should either be dropped or changed to check the Docker tag format so its behavior matches its name.

The validation only checks that the release tag is non-empty; it does not guard against malformed tags containing whitespace or characters that Docker would reject, so a stricter check such as a regex match could be added for more defensive validation.

Every 'released' event also pushes the ':latest' tag, so publishing a patch release on an older release line (for example 1.9.1 after 2.0.0 has already shipped) would point ':latest' back at the older build.

The 'Validate release tag' step checks for a value that cannot be empty in this context, since tag_name is a required field on a published release and the job only runs when action is 'released', so the check is ineffective. It also fails to catch tag values with characters Docker rejects, such as '/', '+' or spaces, which pass validation but later cause build-push-action to fail with an invalid reference format error.

The concurrency group is keyed on github.ref rather than the release payload; if the motivation for this change is that github.ref cannot be trusted on release events, the same concern would apply here, though in practice github.ref is refs/tags/<tag> on these events so it is likely fine.

The empty-tag guard step can never fail: the job only runs for release events where github.event.action == 'released', and a GitHub release always has a tag_name, so $RELEASE_TAG cannot be empty and the exit 1 branch is dead code.

The step is named 'Validate release tag' but does not actually validate that the tag is a well-formed Docker tag (matching [A-Za-z0-9_.-], at most 128 characters), which is the one thing that could actually break the image push, so the name promises more than the step does.

A one-line comment should be added above RELEASE_TAG explaining the reason for using github.event.release.tag_name instead of github.ref_name, for example that the release's tag is the source of truth even if the workflow is re-run or triggered from a different ref.
The 'Validate release tag' step runs after the checkout step, so the job could fail sooner if the validation ran before checking out the repository.

The docker-publish-staging job still uses github.ref_name while docker-publish-release now uses github.event.release.tag_name, and without a comment explaining the rationale, a future reader won't know why the two jobs diverge.

The switch from github.ref_name to github.event.release.tag_name has no explanation, even though this file otherwise documents similar choices in comments elsewhere (e.g. ci.yml:6-9, :262-263, :265-267), and the commit message has no body either, leaving no reason for the change even though on release events the two values are identical and produce no visible effect.
A hotfix release built from an older minor version branch would cause the ':latest' tag to move backwards, since tagging logic does not account for release order relative to the tip.
